newsitem.title: USA: Dow rallies to top 6,500 mark for first time.
newsitem.headline: Dow rallies to top 6,500 mark for first time.

text.p: Stocks were broadly higher Monday, and the Dow Jones industrial average crossed the 6,500 level for the first time.
Shortly after 1 p.m. EST, the Dow was up 42.12 points at 6,513.88, beating Friday's record of 6,471.76, which was its 42nd record so far this year.
In the broader market, advances outpaced declines 14-8 on active volume of more than 287 million shares.
The Nasdaq composite index was up 5.16 at 1,279.52 and the Anerican Stock Exchange index was up 0.04 at 590.81.
The market was paced by strong gains in the energy and financial sectors.
"The financials are really leading this market," said Guy Truicko, portfolio manager at Unity Management. "The bond market has laid a nice foundation."
J.P. Morgan & Co., a component of the 30-stock Dow index, rose 1-1/4 to 91-5/8. Citicorp climbed 2 to 108-1/2 and Chase Manhattan Corp. added 2-5/8 at 94-1/8.

Treasuries also posted solid gains, with the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond up 10/32, lowering its yield to 6.42 percent from 6.44 percent at Friday's close. Bond prices and yields move in opposite direction.

Stocks got off to a shaky start, edging lower initially as investors took profits after Friday's rally. The Dow quickly reversed course, however, and by late morning broader indices had followed suit.
Analysts said financial markets were boosted by Wall Street's growing confidence that inflation was in check and by the solid showing by the dollar.

"There's a growing feeling that the low interest rate and low inflation environment scenario could continue well into 1997," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co. "The strong dollar will also help to focus foreign investors on U.S. markets."
The dollar rose to 1.5223 German marks from 1.5073 in late New York trading Friday. It rose to 112.66 Japanese yen from 111.40 Friday.

In economic news, the National Association of Realtors said existing home sales fell to an annual rate of 3.97 million units in October from 4.03 million in September, a slightly steeper decline than expected.

Economists said the data is considered to be a leading indicator for the overall economy and may indicate that growth should remain tepid for the near term, which would be bullish for the bond market.
Among individual stocks, PanEnergy Corp. gained 1-5/8 to 43-7/8 after agreeing to merge with Duke Power Co. for a total of $7.7 billion in stock. Duke Power fell 1-3/4 to 46-1/8.
